title: Senior Software Developer (JCP Core Foundation Licensing and Quotation)
description:
If you want to build and own the systems that decide what JetBrains customers are entitled to use and bill them accurately for it, this is for you. You will focus on designing backend services, keeping complex commercial flows correct, and tackling hard distributed systems challenges on the critical path of every paid request.

About JetBrains

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

What you’ll do

At JetBrains, the Cloud Platform department builds the underlying infrastructure that powers authentication, paid capabilities, usage metering, and accounting. Within this department, the Licensing & Billing team sits right at the center of our commercial model, turning what a customer buys into what they are actually allowed to use, and accounting for that consumption accurately enough to bill on.

The complexity of our entitlement, quota, and metering systems continues to grow. In this role, you will own the correctness and evolution of these backend services, take full ownership of end-to-end data flows, tackle distributed consistency across unreliable upstream systems, and ensure revenue-affecting data migrations happen cleanly without taking services offline.

Day to day, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate backend services that decide what a customer is entitled to and what their usage costs.
  • Own flows end to end, from ingesting licensing and purchase data from upstream systems to enforcing quotas and recording consumption.
  • Evolve our domain model to handle new commercial structures, combining seat-based plans and usage-based models.
  • Design integrations with external systems, ensuring correctness through idempotency, ordering, reconciliation, and eventual consistency.
  • Plan and execute live data migrations using feature flags, dual writes, backfills, and verification at every stage.
  • Build observability into our systems by defining invariants, metrics, and alerts to catch silent divergence before customers do.
  • Design internal APIs with explicit focus on versioning, backward compatibility, and developer experience for other JetBrains teams.
  • Improve system performance and reliability under continuous production load while decommissioning legacy subsystems.
  • Write integration tests against real dependencies and maintain reliable test infrastructure.
  • Investigate production incidents, find root causes, and follow through on lasting fixes.

What you’ll bring

  • An engineer’s dedication to accuracy, especially in domains where system errors have direct financial impact.
  • Pragmatic judgment when designing distributed systems where correctness under unreliable delivery is the main constraint.
  • A habit of trusting metrics, traces, and logs to understand production behavior rather than relying on assumptions.
  • Comfort navigating and simplifying large existing codebases containing legacy decisions.
  • Clear, direct communication skills to agree on API contracts across teams with different priorities.
  • A focus on testing as an essential design tool rather than an afterthought.

What you’ll need

  • A proven track record of building and operating backend services on the JVM platform using Kotlin or Java.
  • A solid working knowledge of relational databases, including transactions, isolation levels, locking, indexing, and live schema migrations (PostgreSQL preferred).
  • A deep understanding of distributed systems patterns, such as idempotency, retry strategies, eventual consistency, and data reconciliation.
  • Practical experience making live data migrations or system changes without downtime using feature flags and staged rollouts.
  • Experience designing versioned, backward-compatible APIs for other engineering teams.
  • Hands-on experience with event-driven architectures and message brokers like Kafka.
  • The ability to diagnose, debug, and resolve production incidents in complex environments.
  • Proficiency in both written and spoken English.

What success looks like

Success in this role means building a bulletproof entitlement and metering foundation that product teams can trust without hesitation. You will have successfully migrated live commercial systems to support new billing models without downtime or data divergence. Silent errors will be caught automatically by system invariants before affecting users, and internal teams will integrate seamlessly with your clean, versioned APIs.

title: Director, Customer Compensation & Policy
description:
About the Role 

Within Global Customer Experience (GCX), our mission is to advance the HelloFresh customer relationship from reactive resolution to proactive, trust-building service. The compensation function sits at the heart of that mission: it is the mechanism through which the business acknowledges failures, restores customer confidence, and, when done well, turns a bad experience into a reason to stay.

The Associate Director, Customer Compensation & Policy is responsible for the global strategy, architecture, and governance of how HelloFresh compensates customers across all markets and brands. This is not a policy maintenance role. It is a strategic function that sits at the intersection of customer economics, operational data, behavioral experimentation, and cross-functional influence.

You will own one of the most financially material and customer-sensitive levers in the business. You will shape a multi-year roadmap and hold peers in Operations, Technology, Finance, and Market Leadership accountable for the quality of inputs that determine how well and how efficiently we recover customer trust.

The ideal candidate brings a rare combination: analytical rigor sharp enough to architect a global compensation engine from first principles, and the executive presence to drive adoption across a complex, multi-market organization without formal authority over most of the people they need to move.

What You'll Own 

 Global Compensation Strategy & Engine Architecture

  • Own the end-to-end strategic vision for how HelloFresh categorizes customer errors and determines compensation across all markets, brands, and contact channels.
  • Lead the design and continuous evolution of the compensation engine: along with Tech, you’ll define the the rules, thresholds, segmentation logic, and automation frameworks that govern recovery decisions at scale.
  • Define the principles that govern trade-offs between customer generosity and cost discipline and translate those principles into operational rules that hold across market complexity and brand variation.
  • Partner with Technology to ensure the compensation engine is scalable, auditable, and capable of supporting dynamic, AI-assisted decisioning as the product evolves.

Experimentation & Behavioral Economics

  • Set the global roadmap for compensation experimentation: A/B testing across offer types, value levels, channel timing, and segmentation variables.
  • Apply behavioral economics frameworks to compensation design understanding how recovery offers shape long-term retention, repurchase behavior, and brand perception, not just immediate satisfaction.
  • Define the measurement framework for experimentation: what constitutes a successful test, what confidence warrants global rollout, and how results are synthesized into durable policy change.
  • Partner with Analytics & Insights to ensure test design, sample integrity, and rollout analysis meet a rigorous standard of evidence.

Financial Stewardship & Cost Governance

  • Own the global compensation P&L line: tracking spend by market, error category, customer segment, and channel — and holding yourself accountable to defined cost-per-incident and avoidable-contact targets.
  • Identify and close financial leakage: cases where compensation is being issued without policy justification, at incorrect values, or at the wrong frequency.
  • Build the reporting infrastructure that makes compensation economics visible to GCX leadership, market GMs, and Finance — with the granularity and context needed to drive decisions.
  • Define the right balance between cost optimization and customer lifetime value investment: not just 'spend less' but 'spend where it earns back.

Fraud Policy & Global Governance

  • Own the global fraud and abuse prevention framework: the policies, detection logic, thresholds, and escalation paths that protect the business without creating friction for genuine customers.
  • Lead the governance rhythm for policy: quarterly reviews, market exception management, escalation adjudication, and framework versioning across a multi-brand, multi-market environment.
  • Act as the final authority on complex, cross-market policy gaps — resolving ambiguity with speed, consistency, and strategic clarity rather than routing decisions upward by default.
  • Maintain global standards while creating principled space for market-level adaptation where local context genuinely requires it.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Stakeholder Accountability

  • Represent the compensation function in senior forums translating customer economics into requirements that peers in Operations, Technology, Finance, and Market GMs must respond to.
  • Hold cross-functional partners accountable for the upstream data quality, operational accuracy, and system reliability that the compensation engine depends on.
  • Drive adoption of policy changes across markets and brands, building communication and change management plans that make new frameworks land — not just launch.
  • Influence at VP and Director level across multiple functions; escalate only strategic blockers, not routine alignment.

What You'll Bring 

Education

  • MBA or equivalent postgraduate qualification required.
  • Undergraduate degree in Economics, Business, Engineering, or a quantitative discipline.

Experience

  • 8–12 years of progressive experience in customer strategy, pricing, operations, or a directly adjacent domain with meaningful exposure to global, multi-market environments.
  • Demonstrated track record of owning a financially significant operational lever and managing it with both analytical precision and strategic judgment.
  • Prior experience leading and developing teams; comfort operating as a senior individual contributor and a people leader simultaneously.
  • Background in subscription commerce, logistics, or consumer-facing operations strongly preferred. Familiarity with the economics of customer recovery in high-volume, low-margin environments is a distinct advantage.

Technical & Analytical

  • Advanced proficiency in SQL and data analysis; able to build and pressure-test the analytical models that underpin policy decisions without delegating the logic to others.
  • Fluency with experimentation methodology: test design, statistical significance, holdout analysis, and the translation of results into policy not just reporting.
  • Experience working with or alongside engineering teams to define product and system requirements for rules-based or AI-assisted decisioning tools.
  • Comfort with financial modeling: building the business case for compensation investment, forecasting spend impact, and tracking actuals against plan.

Leadership & Influence

  • Senior executive presence: able to walk into a GM, COO, or CFO conversation with a clear point of view, defend it under pressure, and leave with alignment.
  • A credible voice with peers and upward stakeholders not because of title, but because of the quality of analysis and clarity of communication.
  • Structured and decisive under ambiguity: able to make a defensible call with incomplete information and adjust as evidence develops.
  • Genuinely collaborative across markets and functions able to hold people to standards without damaging the relationships needed to sustain them.

title: Senior Design Engineer, Design System
description:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

Why this role matters

At Celonis, design has to scale across a complex, enterprise-grade process intelligence platform, and increasingly, it has to scale to machines as well as people. AI coding agents now generate a growing share of the UI our engineers ship, and our design system is the contract that keeps that output on-brand, accessible, and consistent.

This role sits at the intersection of design, engineering, and product, with a strong emphasis on craft, usability, and scalability. You'll design and build the system itself, owning interaction decisions and front-end architecture, and translating complex process data and AI-driven behaviors into intuitive, high-performance experiences. It's a senior role: you'll often operate with minimal design oversight, set standards, lead initiatives, and mentor others while staying deeply hands-on in both design and code.

About the team

You'll join the team that owns Celonis's design system and the operations behind how design gets done. We sit at the intersection of design and engineering, and we treat the system as a living product with real users, internal designers, product engineers, and the AI agents that now consume it.

What you'll do

  • Design and build production components in Angular and TypeScript, our design system is built in Angular and we may adopt React over time, on a foundation of rock-solid HTML and CSS (semantic markup, ARIA, and modern CSS custom properties driving design tokens).

  • Make the system agent-ready: maintain tokens-as-code in the W3C DTCG format (Style Dictionary or similar) and structure component metadata, docs, and APIs so AI coding agents can consume them as reliable context.

  • Use AI tooling daily (Figma Make, v0, Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, or similar), applying senior design and engineering judgment to critique and correct the output.
  • Lead system initiatives and mentor designers and engineers contributing to it.

What you'll bring

  • Strong Figma fluency and comfort moving fluidly between design and code.
  • Demonstrated accessibility expertise (WCAG 2.2) implemented in code.
  • Hands-on fluency with AI design and coding tools, and an opinionated, responsible point of view on using them.
  • A strong product mindset and bias toward ownership, plus the communication and leadership of a senior IC.

Bonus points

  • Experience building or integrating MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers e.g. the Figma Dev Mode MCP server or a custom design-system MCP server.
  • Experience building evals for AI-generated UI, or writing specs/prompts for AI generation.
  • Background working on complex, data-dense, or real-time interfaces (a strong fit for our process-intelligence product).
  • Token-pipeline experience with Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, or equivalent.

How we work

This is a senior role: you'll own major areas of the system with full autonomy, design and ship with a high bar for craft, set the standards others build to, lead initiatives, and mentor. We pair design craft with engineering depth and high curiosity about AI, building a system that's faster and safer for humans and agents alike.

  • Global Inclusion & Belonging: Find community through our Inclusion Think Tank and participate in our annual Inclusion Days, ensuring every voice is heard and valued.
  • Value-Driven Impact: Join a mission-led organization where our core values—Live for Customer Value, The Best Team Wins, We Own It, and Earth Is Our Future—drive every decision.

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI, empowering organizations to analyze, design, and operate AI-driven processes.
